channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Alford to produce docs in HPE matter
item.description: A California federal judge has said Roger Alford must hand over communications related to Hewlett Packard Enterprise’s settlement with the Department of Justice, including those from after his firing from the agency.

item.title: DOJ sues OhioHealth for restricting narrower health plans
item.description: The Department of Justice has accused one of Ohio’s leading healthcare systems of using its market power to prohibit health insurers from offering cheaper plans to patients.

item.title: Everybody talks: The Tipline for 20 February 2026
item.description: It started with a whisper. Live Nation thinks the summary judgment ruling — which allowed most of the Department of Justice’s case to continue but axed key claims related to major concert venues — doomed its bid for a Ticketmaster divestiture. “It’s time to move on,” wrote in-house counsel Dan Wall in a blog post. item.title: FTC only seeking to block mergers in federal court, Ferguson says
item.description: Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson has signalled the agency will only fight pending mergers in federal court, a change that aligns its merger challenge process with the Department of Justice following years of legal challenges.

item.title: Transaction declined: The Briefing for 23 February 2026
item.description: Visa has failed to convince Mexico’s National Antitrust Commission to approve its bid for a majority stake in one of the country’s largest card payment processors – marking the first time the newly established competition watchdog has publicly opposed a merger. item.title: World Snooker Tour organiser resists disclosure in UK standalone claim
item.description: The UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has criticised World Snooker for attacking the merits of a standalone claim brought by a company partly owned by professional snooker player Ronnie O’Sullivan as a way of resisting disclosure.

item.title: Getty, Shutterstock still deciding on UK remedies strategy following DOJ greenlight
item.description: Getty Images and Shutterstock have not yet finalised their approach to remedying UK competition concerns about their £3 billion tie-up following confirmation that the US Department of Justice has unconditionally approved the deal.

item.title: Call for reinforcements: The Tipline for 23 February 2026
item.description: The Department of Justice is hiring. The Antitrust Division listed 14 job openings on Monday for attorneys to work on civil and criminal matters in Chicago, San Francisco and Washington, DC. Meanwhile, Live Nation continues its push to scrap the division’s monopolisation suit, arguing that last week’s summary judgment order spoils what remains of the case.

item.title: UGG maker hit with monopolisation suit
item.description: The manufacturer of UGG boots weaponised hundreds of “sham” trade dress lawsuits to exclude competition and maintain supracompetitive prices, a rival footwear manufacturer has alleged.

item.title: US enforcers drafting collaboration guidelines
item.description: The US antitrust agencies have requested public input on new guidelines outlining permissible collaboration between competitors, following the Biden Administration's withdrawal of the previous document in 2024.
